post.summary: Take durable ownership of one inbound webhook delivery.
post.description:
Everything the caller is answered with is decided before any routing runs:
the delivery is verified, parsed, and written to the Adapter delivery seam,
and only then acknowledged. A 200 therefore means the backend owns the delivery,
not that a Task exists — the Task is created later, by the worker, out of the
record this wrote. Anything that failed to record reaches the caller as a
failure so its own retry is the recovery path.

Deactivated loops are rejected before admission. A Loop can also be
paused or resynced after admission; the worker rechecks runnable state and
then terminates the durable delivery without creating a Task.

200.description: The delivery is owned by the backend. Names the delivery, not a Task.

post.description:
Flips a `Closed` task back to `Open` so it can be started and chatted with
again. No sandbox is provisioned here — that happens on the next `start` or
inbound message, at which point the sandbox restores any retained S3 state
(Claude transcript + `s3`-mode workspace) keyed by `task_id`. Whether that
state still exists depends on `SANDBOX_RETAIN_STORAGE_ON_CLOSE` having been
set when the task was closed; if not, the task reopens with a fresh
sandbox. External bindings deactivated on close are left inactive.

reaper — the sandbox stays alive until explicitly stopped). `inactive_ttl_days`

omit a field to leave that TTL unchanged. At least one must be provided.

post.description:
With `isBot: true`, resolves the App's `{slug}[bot]` identity via
`GitHubAppRegistry`, then inserts both the `users` row and a matching
`provider_tokens` row with `auth_method = 'github_app_installation'` so
credential resolution transparently mints installation tokens for tasks
that `run_as_user_id = <bot id>`.

With `isBot: false`, creates a human user with a local password. Available
only under local password auth — OAuth deployments create users on callback.

body are changed.

patch.summary:
Override a git-synced workspace. Sets `source = "manual"` so that git sync
skips this workspace going forward. Provenance fields are preserved.
Use `POST /{id}/reset-git` to re-enable git sync.

200.description: Workspace overridden; source set to manual

post.summary: Discard a workspace's local override and take its run-config from git again.
post.description:
Implemented as a re-sync of just this workspace rather than a flag flip, so
`source` only returns to `"git"` when the repository still declares the
entry — a workspace can never end up claiming git provenance while holding
config git never produced.

200.description: Re-sync attempted; `resynced` reports whether it took effect

400.description: Workspace was never synced from git

ActivationReach.description: Who an activation applies to: everyone, or the calling user alone.

AdapterConnectionResponse.description: One adapter connection, describing a transport/auth scope.

AdapterSendRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/v1/adapters/send` — generic adapter pass-through send.

connectionId.description:
Optional connection ID. When omitted, the backend picks the single
accessible connection of `adapter` kind, or returns an error if zero
or more than one match.

taskId.description:
Optional task to bind this send to. When set, a `task_bindings` row
is created so future `moat reply` calls thread under this destination.

bindingId.description:
ID of the binding created/updated by this send. Present only when
`task_id` was provided on the request.

externalId.description: Adapter-specific external message ID (e.g. Slack `ts`, Linear comment ID).

subjectKind.description:
Binding `subject_kind` produced by the adapter (e.g. `slack_thread`,
`linear_comment`). Surfaced so callers can correlate with bindings.

AdminResetPasswordRequest.description:
PUT /api/v1/users/{login}/password request (admin reset — no current
password required).

`Debug` is hand-written to redact `new_password`.

mustChangePassword.description: Force a password change on next login. Defaults to `false`.

AdminUpdateUserRequest.description:
Body for PATCH /api/v1/users/{login}.

`None` means the field was omitted and should remain unchanged.
`Some(None)` means the caller explicitly sent `null` and the column should be cleared.

AgentEventPayload.description:
Agent event payload — typed shape for `EventType::Agent` events.

Agent payloads are pass-through from the sandbox (Claude CLI output).
This struct is primarily for OpenAPI schema generation; at runtime the
backend continues to forward `serde_json::Value` payloads.

message.description: For "message" subtype: the Claude SDK assistant message.

toolName.description: For "pending_response" subtype: the tool being invoked.

AgentStatus.description: Observed Agent lifecycle while its Sandbox is ready.

AllowedPrompt.description: A tool/prompt that the agent requests permission to execute.

ApiKeyCreateResponse.description: POST /api/v1/auth/api-keys response (includes the full key, shown once).

ApiMessage.description: A message in the Anthropic API format.

AskUserQuestionInput.description: Input payload for the AskUserQuestion tool.

AuthModeResponse.description:
GET /api/v1/auth/mode response.

A dedicated endpoint rather than a field on `SessionResponse`: `/auth/me`
401s for anonymous callers, and the login page is anonymous by definition.

loginUrl.description: Where to send the browser to start an OAuth login. `None` in password mode.

BackgroundProcess.description:
A live background process (a `run_in_background` job or ad-hoc daemon) still
running in the sandbox after the agent went idle.

BackgroundWatchJobInfo.description:
Watch that re-triggers the agent once the `run_in_background` jobs captured
at the end of a turn have finished (subprocess mode only).

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
PUT /api/v1/auth/password request (change own password).

`Debug` is hand-written to redact both passwords.

closeChildren.description:
Whether descendant tasks created by this task should also be closed.
Required when the task has children; optional for leaf tasks.

authMethod.description: "device_code" | "auth_json" | "api_key" — which save path produced the row.

email.description: Email reported by ChatGPT account on the id_token (device-code flow only).

needsReconnect.description:
True when the stored credential hit a permanent refresh failure and
the user must sign in again. Absent when no credential exists.

Connection.description:
A single external connection (one task binding) with its decoded label,
external status, and message tally.

active.description:
Whether this connection still routes inbound events. `false` once the
task closes — the binding is kept for history but stops listening.

deactivatedAt.description:
RFC3339 timestamp of when the connection was deactivated; `None` while
active.

incoming.description: Inbound message count for this connection.

kind.description:
Decoded connection kind: `github_pr` | `linear_issue` | `slack_thread`
| the raw `subject_kind` for anything else.

lastEventAt.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the last event seen on the binding.

mergeableState.description:
GitHub PR mergeable state: clean | dirty | blocked | behind | unstable |
has_hooks | draft. `dirty` means merge conflicts. `None` when not
computed or not a PR.

outgoing.description: Outgoing message count for this connection.

reviewDecision.description:
GitHub PR review decision: approved | changes_requested |
review_required | dismissed | commented. `None` for non-PR connections
or PRs with no review recorded yet.

status.description:
Display status string (GitHub: open/merged/closed/draft; Linear: state
name). `None` when no status has been persisted/fetched yet.

statusUpdatedAt.description: RFC3339 timestamp of when the status was last refreshed.

url.description: Web URL for the connected subject, when derivable.

ContainerDiagnostics.description: Container-level diagnostics for troubleshooting sandbox issues.

cpuMillicores.description: CPU usage in millicores (from K8s Metrics API, if available)

memoryMb.description: Memory usage in megabytes (from K8s Metrics API, if available)

ContentBlock.description: A content block within an API message.

adapterKind.description: Adapter implementation kind, such as `slack`, `github`, or `webhook`.

connectionKind.description: Transport/auth style for this adapter, e.g. `bot_api`, `org_webhook`.

externalAccountId.description: External account/workspace/org identifier for this connection.

oneOf.description: Access scope for this connection. Defaults to `user`.

sourceName.description: Optional human-readable name for the connection.

webhookSecret.description: HMAC secret used to verify inbound webhooks for this workspace.

name.description: Human-readable name. Required and must not be blank.

label.description:
What to call the device being paired. Becomes the name of the API key
the exchange mints, which is how it is recognized and revoked later.

CreatePluginRequest.description: Request to register a new plugin.

CreateRepositoryRequest.description:
A repository is a connection to a git repo. Run-configuration lives on the
workspace, not here.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort for the first turn, in the agent's own vocabulary
(`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` for Claude,
`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` for Codex). Omit to leave the agent on
its own default.

repositoryId.description:
The repository to run the task against. Optional when `workspace_id` is
supplied — the workspace's primary repository is used instead. At least
one of `repository_id` / `workspace_id` is required.

workspaceId.description:
Explicit workspace to run the task in. When set, its repositories drive
the task (workspace wins over `repository_id`). When unset, the task
derives the repository's deterministic shadow workspace, keeping the
single-repo path unchanged.

CreateUserRequest.description:
POST /api/v1/users request.

With `isBot: true`, creates a bot user backed by a configured GitHub App:
the server resolves the App's `{slug}[bot]` identity from
`GitHubAppRegistry` and writes both the `users` row and the matching
`provider_tokens` row atomically. `githubAppKey` is required in this mode.

With `isBot: false`, creates a human user with a local password. Only
available when the server runs local password auth; `login` and `password`
are required in this mode.

`Debug` is hand-written to redact `password`.

githubAppKey.description:
Registry key of a configured GitHub App (e.g. `"dev-bot"`). Required
when `isBot` is `true`.

isBot.description: `true` for a GitHub App bot, `false` for a local password user.

login.description: Login handle for a local user. Required when `isBot` is `false`.

mustChangePassword.description: Force a password change on first login. Defaults to `false`.

password.description: Initial password for a local user. Required when `isBot` is `false`.

repos.description: Repository placements. May be empty (a blank/scratch workspace).

EffectivePluginResponse.description: What the calling user actually gets, after resolution.

skillNames.description: Never empty — a plugin with no picked skills is not delivered at all.

ElementContextData.description: Data for an element context (selected UI component).

ErrorBody.description: Standard JSON error body. All API errors MUST use this shape.

EventType.description:
Top-level event types.

Serializes to the exact strings the frontend `EventTypeSchema` expects.
Renamed: "environment" → "sandbox" to avoid confusion with K8s environments.

ExitPlanModeInput.description: Input payload for the ExitPlanMode tool.

device_pairing.description:
Whether the settings dialog offers to pair a device.

Not an `FF_*` variable of its own: pairing is the bootstrap half of the
T3 compatibility routes, and a code is worth nothing on a deployment
that does not mount them. So it reports whether *they* are on.

FeedbackResponse.description: Response shape for a single feedback row.

FeedbackSource.description: Submitter of a feedback row — derived from auth context on the server.

FeedbackSurface.description: Where in the UI/CLI the feedback originated.

FileContentResponse.description: File content response with optional git change info.

FileContextData.description:
Data for a file attachment context. Filled in by the backend at read
time from `file_metadata`; senders supply only `reference_id`.

FileNameMatchDto.description: A file name match in the search results.

FileTreeNodeDto.description: A node in the file tree (file or directory).

FileTreeResponse.description: File tree response with git change summary.

FollowTaskResponse.description: Response for follow/unfollow endpoints, reporting the resulting state.

following.description: Whether the requesting user follows the task after the operation.

hasMore.description: Whether older messages exist beyond the returned page.

nextBeforeId.description: Cursor for fetching the next older page; `None` when no older rows remain.

totalCount.description:
Number of messages in this response. Required by the upstream
moatless-swarm-ui CLI which deserializes against a `totalCount: usize`
field; omitting it breaks `moat messages list <task_id>`.

botLogin.description:
The bot login this App would have, as GitHub reported it when the App
was last proved.

botUserId.description: The Bot user staffing this App, when one has been created.

deploymentConfigured.description:
True for the App the deployment configures for signing in. It is listed
so admins can see it, and it cannot be rotated or removed from here.

GitHubAppRegistrationResponse.description: What GitHub confirmed about an App that was just registered or rotated.

botLogin.description:
The bot login this App would have. Creating the Bot user is a separate
act — an App that only reaches repositories never runs as anyone.

hasPatOverride.description: True when a GitHub-OAuth user has an active PAT override.

GitSummaryDto.description: Git change summary across the workspace.

GithubBindPrRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/bind` — bind an
existing PR to a task without mutating GitHub.

GithubBindPrResponse.description: Response for binding an existing PR.

bindingId.description: Set when the task binding upsert succeeded.

GithubCommentRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments` —
post a comment on a PR or issue (GitHub's issues API covers both).

taskId.description:
Task to bind the PR/issue to and dedup the comment's webhook echo
against. See [`GithubCreatePrRequest::task_id`].

GithubCommentResponse.description:
Response for comment creation (top-level comments and threaded
review-comment replies alike).

bindingId.description:
Set only when the request included a `task_id` and the binding upsert
succeeded.

base.description: Base branch. Defaults to the repository's default branch when omitted.

head.description:
Head branch the PR is created from. The CLI infers this from the
current git branch when the agent omits `--head`.

taskId.description:
Task to bind the created PR to. When provided, a `task_bindings` row
is upserted so inbound PR comments route back to this task, and a
`Moatless task: <url>` footer is appended to the PR body.

bindingId.description:
Set only when the request included a `task_id` and the binding upsert
succeeded.

GithubReplyRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies`
— threaded reply to a PR review (inline) comment.

taskId.description:
Task to bind the PR to and dedup the reply's webhook echo against.
See [`GithubCreatePrRequest::task_id`].

ImageSource.description: Image source within a content block.

bind.description:
Force the parent issue into a reply target even when no binding exists
yet. A comment on an already-bound issue refreshes its binding
regardless; this flag covers a proactive comment on an unbound issue.
Defaults to `false`. See [`LinearIssueCreateRequest::bind`].

taskId.description:
Task to associate the parent issue with. See
[`LinearIssueCreateRequest::task_id`].

assignee.description:
Assignee email, display name, or UUID. `"me"` resolves to the
authenticated agent (the workspace OAuth viewer).

bind.description:
Opt the created issue into being a reply target: when `true` (and
`task_id` is set) a `task_bindings` row with `subject_kind =
"linear_issue"` is inserted so future comments on the issue route back
to the task and `moat messages reply` can post here. Filing alone does
NOT bind — this defaults to `false`.

priority.description: Linear priority: 0 No-priority, 1 Urgent, 2 High, 3 Normal, 4 Low.

reporter.description:
Real Linear user to record as the issue reporter. Accepts email,
display name, UUID, or "me". Added as a subscriber and mentioned in
the description (Linear has no settable creator/reporter field).

taskId.description:
Task to associate the created issue with (records a clickable Moatless
attachment on the issue for traceability).

team.description:
Team key (e.g. `SP`) or UUID. Optional — defaults to the only team
the connection's user can see when omitted.

templateId.description: Optional template UUID applied before the explicit fields.

LinearIssueResponse.description:
Common envelope for all typed responses. `data` is the raw Linear
subobject (e.g. issue, comment); `binding_id` is set only when the
request included a `task_id` and a `task_bindings` row was inserted.

parent.description:
Parent issue identifier or UUID. Pass `"null"` (literal string) or
the JSON `null` value to clear the parent.

LinearLookupResponse.description:
Response for `/lookup`. Returns at most one match (the first
case-insensitive name hit).

LinearOkResponse.description: Response for label add/remove (no body content).

LiveStatus.description: The complete live status of a Task's Sandbox and Agent.

name.description:
Human-readable name. Required on every Loop — for Git-declared Loops it
comes from the `name` frontmatter of `.moatless/loops/<dir>/LOOP.md`.

inactiveTtlDays.description:
Per-Loop inactivity TTL in days. `None` means "inherit the global
default" (`TASK_INACTIVE_TIMEOUT_DAYS`). Flows into `tasks.inactive_ttl_days`
when this Loop spawns a task.

oneOf.description:
`None` for schedule loops (no return-channel binding) and for
adapter-event tasks that lost their original binding.

LoopSyncSkip.description:
One loop that was skipped during a sync, with a human-readable reason
(e.g. "no github connection for org acme").

LoopSyncSummary.description: Summary of reconciling a repo's `.moatless/loops/` into Loop tables.

approvalsRevoked.description: Existing Git-synced Loops whose approval was revoked.

overridesSkipped.description: Manual overrides or deletion tombstones preserved during repository sync.

removed.description: Loops removed because their directory is gone.

skipped.description: Loops that were present but not synced, with reasons.

warnings.description: Non-fatal authoring warnings, including ignored Git authority fields.

data.description:
Backend-resolved metadata. Senders may pass an empty default — the
backend overwrites it from `file_metadata` before persisting.

MessageContextInput.description: A context attached to a message, discriminated by `type`.

externalId.description:
Provider-specific reaction id, when the API returns one
(e.g. GitHub reaction id, Linear reaction UUID).

MoatlessToolName.description: All available Moatless tool names injected into the agent sandbox.

PairingCodeResponse.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/pairing-codes response.

The code is readable here and nowhere else — only its hash is stored — so a
caller that loses this response asks for another code rather than recovering
this one.

code.description: The code to type into the client being paired.

PasswordLoginRequest.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/password/login request.

`Debug` is hand-written to redact `password`.

enabled.description: Toggle the secret active/inactive without touching its value.

PendingMessageItem.description: A pending message item (user message or result message).

messageText.description: What the person wrote, as text.

syncedVersion.description:
What the source called its current state at the last successful sync.
Absent until a first sync succeeds.

PluginSkillResponse.description: One skill inside a plugin, as stored at the plugin's synced version.

PreviewUrlContextData.description: Data for a preview URL context.

ProviderConnection.description:
Connection state for an external provider (OAuth app, GitHub App, PAT, …).

`connected = false` indicates the frontend should prompt the user to
reconnect: either no token is stored, or the most recent refresh attempt
failed.

connected.description:
True when a usable token exists and, for refreshable tokens, the most
recent refresh succeeded.

login.description: Provider login (e.g. GitHub username) when available.

Question.description: A question presented to the user during agent interaction.

QuestionOption.description: An option within a question presented to the user.

appId.description: GitHub's own numeric id for the App.

githubAppKey.description: Short stable name the App will be known by, chosen at registration.

privateKeyPem.description:
PEM-encoded signing key. Proved against GitHub before anything is
stored, and never returned by any read path afterwards.

orphanedBotUsers.description:
Bot users that named this App and can no longer obtain a token. They
are left in place so past work stays attributed, and named here so the
consequence is not silent.

ReplyTargetDescriptor.description: One outbound destination returned by task reply APIs.

flagHint.description: CLI flag the caller should add to disambiguate, e.g. `"--binding bind_xyz"`.

kind.description: Target category, currently `"binding"` for canonical task bindings.

label.description: Human-readable label such as `"slack source:C123"` or `"github pr:owner/repo#42"`.

externalId.description: Provider-specific external id of the reply we posted, when the API returns one.

accessStatus.description:
Provider reachability of `remote_url`: `unchecked` | `ok` | `not_found`
| `forbidden` | `error`. Stamped when the repo is auto-created by a
git-synced workspace.

ResetGitWorkspaceResponse.description:
Response for `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/reset-git`.

The workspace only returns to `source = "git"` when the re-sync actually
found it still declared in the repository, so `resynced` reports whether the
reset took effect.

error.description:
Why the re-sync did not take effect (unreachable provider, or the entry
is no longer declared in the config file). `None` when `resynced`.

resynced.description: Whether the workspace was reclaimed from git during this call.

buildCache.description:
Per-repository size cap for the transient `build-cache` emptyDir mounted
at `/opt/moatless/build-cache` (e.g. "40Gi"). Use with workspace env vars
such as `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/opt/moatless/build-cache/target` for large
build artifacts that should not fill the workspace volume. Exceeding the
cap gets the pod **evicted** by the kubelet. When unset, the global
`K8S_SANDBOX_BUILD_CACHE_SIZE` default applies.

buildCacheMode.description:
Storage backend for the `build-cache` volume mounted at
`/opt/moatless/build-cache`:
- `"emptyDir"` (default) — node-local emptyDir capped by `buildCache`.
- `"node"` — node-local hostPath under `K8S_SANDBOX_CACHE_HOST_ROOT`.
  Kubernetes does not enforce `buildCache` as a size cap for this mode.

buildCacheScope.description:
Scope for `buildCacheMode: "node"`:
- `"task"` (default) — per-task hostPath, cleaned up with the task.
- `"node"` — shared by all sandboxes scheduled on the same node.

dockerStorage.description:
Per-repository size cap for the `dind` sidecar's `/var/lib/docker`
emptyDir (e.g. "50Gi"). Only meaningful for repos with `dockerAccess`
and `dockerStorageMode: "emptyDir"`. Exceeding the cap gets the pod
**evicted** by the kubelet, wiping all dind container data. When unset,
the global `K8S_SANDBOX_DOCKER_DIND_STORAGE_SIZE` default applies.

dockerStorageMode.description:
Storage backend for the `dind` sidecar's `/var/lib/docker`:
- `"node"` (default) — best-effort node-local hostPath. Docker layers,
  images, and volumes survive stop/start only on the same node.
- `"emptyDir"` — node-local emptyDir capped by `dockerStorage`.

storage.description:
Per-repository workspace storage size override (e.g. "8Gi"). Sizes the
per-task PVC (`ebs`) and node-local emptyDir (`ephemeral`/`s3`) tiers.
The `node` hostPath tier is bounded by node disk capacity instead. When
unset, the global `K8S_SANDBOX_STORAGE_SIZE` default applies. Never copied
into container resource specs.

storageMode.description:
Per-repository storage tier. One of [`STORAGE_MODES`]:
- `"ebs"` (default) — a per-task EBS PVC mounted at `/opt/moatless`,
  surviving pod restarts.
- `"ephemeral"` — a node-local emptyDir, no PVC; transcripts persist only
  via the S3 sync, the workspace does not survive the pod.
- `"s3"` — a node-local emptyDir plus a direct git-working-tree sync to S3,
  giving workspace persistence without an EBS attach/detach per restart.
- `"node"` — a best-effort node-local hostPath. The workspace survives
  stop/start only when Kubernetes schedules the task back onto the same node.

When unset, the deployment-wide default applies
(`K8S_SANDBOX_DEFAULT_STORAGE_MODE`, itself defaulting to `"ebs"`).
Unknown values are ignored (treated as unset).

ResourcesEventPayload.description: Resources event payload — typed shape for `EventType::Resources` events.

privateKeyPem.description:
The replacement signing key. Proved before the stored one is replaced,
so a bad key leaves the App exactly as it was.

RoutingMode.description: Loop routing mode for message-to-task mapping.

RuntimeEvent.description:
A provider-agnostic runtime event associated with a sandbox.

In K8s mode, these are sourced from K8s Event objects (FailedScheduling,
BackOff, Pulling, etc.). Docker mode can populate from `docker events`.

count.description: Number of times this event has occurred

SandboxDesiredState.description: Persisted application intent for a task's sandbox lifecycle.

SandboxEventPayload.description:
Sandbox event payload — typed payload for sandbox lifecycle events.

Used by the pod watcher and provider to publish structured events
instead of raw `serde_json::Value`.

disruptionReason.description:
Why the pod was disrupted, from
`pod.status.conditions[DisruptionTarget].reason` (PreemptionByScheduler |
DeletionByTaintManager | TerminationByKubelet | EvictionByEvictionAPI |
DeletionByPodGC), falling back to `pod.status.reason`.

exitCode.description:
Exit code of the terminated sandbox container, when known.

Lets consumers distinguish OOM (137) from an application crash (1) or a
graceful SIGTERM (143). `#[serde(default)]` keeps old events readable.

initiator.description:
Who caused an intentional stop: "reaper" | "user" | "close" | "restart"
| "crash_autostop" | "eviction". Null for events that aren't stops.

nodeName.description:
Node the pod was scheduled on (`pod.spec.node_name`). Enables node-level
correlation of otherwise-unrelated tasks that stopped together.

pendingSeconds.description:
Seconds the pod spent `Pending` before it was scheduled onto a node.
Attached to `pod_scheduled` events so slow scheduling is readable directly.

terminatedReason.description:
K8s termination reason of the sandbox container (e.g. "OOMKilled",
"Error", "Completed"), when known.

SandboxStatus.description:
Sandbox status — valid status values for sandbox lifecycle events.

These match the frontend `SandboxStatus` values.

SandboxStatusFullResponse.description: Full sandbox status response to frontend (matches TS SandboxStatusFullResponse)

backgroundProcesses.description:
Live background processes (`run_in_background` jobs, ad-hoc daemons) still
running in the sandbox. Empty when idle with no background work.

currentSandboxImage.description:
Image the currently-provisioned sandbox container is running, read from
the live Deployment/container. `None` when no sandbox exists yet.

imageUpToDate.description:
`true` when `current_sandbox_image` matches `latest_sandbox_image`.
`None` when either image is unknown (e.g. no sandbox provisioned).

latestSandboxImage.description:
Image a fresh (re)deploy would use for the sandbox container: the
per-repo `docker_image` override when set, otherwise the configured
default. Compare against `current_sandbox_image` to know whether a
redeploy would change the image.

oneOf.description:
Desired sandbox lifecycle intent recorded on the task
(`running`/`stopped`/`removed`). Reflects the last user/system action,
independent of the live pod phase. `None` when it can't be resolved.

SandboxStopReason.description: Reason the persisted sandbox intent moved away from `running`.

ScheduledJobInfo.description: Snapshot of one scheduled job currently registered in the sandbox.

ScheduledJobKind.description: Per-kind payload for a scheduled job.

Scope.description:
Access scope for repositories, tasks, integrations, and credentials.

Reads: `global` is readable by every authenticated user; `user` only by
its owner (and admins). Control: `global` is admin-managed; `user` is
owner-managed. Task `visibility = 'public'` additionally grants
read/interact on tasks — never control.

SearchByNameRequest.description: Request body for searching files by name.

SearchByNameResponse.description: Response for searching files by name.

SecretSource.description: Where a secret value is stored.

SendDmRequest.description: Send a DM to a user via an external provider.

task_id.description: Optional task to associate the DM binding with.

binding_id.description: The created or updated task_binding id.

conversationId.description: External DM conversation ID opened by the adapter.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort for the turn, in the agent's own vocabulary
(`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` for Claude,
`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` for Codex). Omit to leave the agent on
its own default.

sourceTaskId.description: Task ID of the sender (set automatically when sent from within a sandbox).

startFresh.description:
When true, the next agent run starts a fresh session instead of resuming.
Per-message and cleared after send.

uuid.description:
Persisted `uuid` of the user Message, so the client can reconcile its
optimistic entry with the later `message.upsert`. `None` on the
tool-response branch, which produces no single user Message.

dockerImage.description: Per-server Docker image. Falls back to sandbox_image if not set.

oneOf.description:
Per-server resource requests/limits. Falls back to the repo-wide
`resources` when unset. Only `requests`/`limits` apply; storage/cache
fields are repo-wide and ignored here.

ServerConfigResponse.description: Result of a live server config change or restart.

configOverride.description: The override after the call — empty when it was reset.

generation.description: Sidecar restart generation after the call.

ServerEntry.description: Single server entry in the workspace status response

message.description:
Human-readable contextual detail (e.g. "ContainerCreating", "CrashLoopBackOff").
Always set by the publisher. `#[serde(default)]` handles old events without this field.

ServerOverride.description:
A live override of one preview server's start command and env.

Whole-state, not a delta: callers always send the complete set to the
sandbox, which never merges.

env.description: Env entries exported after `server.env`, so they win over it.

startCommand.description:
Replaces the server's configured start command. `None` = use the
workspace's.

unsetEnv.description:
Keys to remove — the only way to drop a variable the container spec
injected, since sourcing an env file can add but never remove.

ServerOverrideEntry.description: One server's override as it currently exists on the workspace volume.

generation.description: The counter the sidecar watches; `0` means it has never been restarted.

ServerOverridesResponse.description:
Every override in effect on a task. Servers with no override are omitted.

Read from the sandbox's workspace volume, which is the only place an
override exists — a stopped sandbox cannot answer this.

ServerStatusResponse.description: Server status response proxied from sandbox pod.

ServerSubType.description:
Server sub-types — server container lifecycle.

`Failed` covers all error conditions (was: Failed, Error, Timeout — consolidated).

providers.description:
Connection state for each external provider (GitHub, etc.). Empty when
no authenticated user. The frontend uses this to surface reconnect
prompts when a provider token has been revoked or failed to refresh.

oneOf.description:
What the environment still needs before it can do its job. Populated
only by `GET /api/v1/auth/me`; absent on login and profile-update
responses, which the frontend treats as "nothing to report".

SetActivationRequest.description: Turn a plugin, or one skill inside it, on or off.

skillName.description: Omit to mean the whole plugin.

SetProviderIdRequest.description: Set or replace the provider-specific user ID for a moatless user.

provider_user_id.description: Provider-specific user ID (e.g. Slack user ID "U0893GU35RV").

SetupAction.description:
A remediation step the frontend can offer. `target` is machine-readable:
a settings-section id, an in-app route, or an absolute URL, per `kind`.

SetupRequirement.description: One thing the environment needs before it can do its job.

actions.description:
Remediation steps, most-preferred first. Empty when satisfied.
Admin-only actions are omitted for non-admin callers, so the frontend
never has to re-derive who may do what.

SetupRequirementId.description:
Which requirement this is. `Unknown` exists so an older client (notably the
`moat` CLI, which deserializes `SessionResponse`) doesn't hard-fail against
a newer server; the backend never constructs it.

SetupRequirementStatus.description:
Tri-state because "configured but unusable" needs different copy from
"never configured": a `secret_ref` row whose secret is gone is `Broken`,
and telling that user to "connect GitHub" would be wrong.

SetupSeverity.description:
A closed vocabulary: a new value here is a real contract change the
frontend should fail to compile against rather than silently ignore.

SetupStatus.description: Environment-setup state for the current user.

requirements.description:
Every evaluated requirement, satisfied ones included, so the frontend
can render a full checklist as well as a nag banner.

SkillResponse.description: Single skill discovered from a `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` file.

StreamEvent.description:
SSE event envelope — the shape of events streamed to the frontend.

This is the canonical wire format for all SSE events. The frontend
receives this shape and dispatches on `event_type` + `sub_type`.

SubagentStatus.description:
Status of a spawned subagent, derived from the outer `Agent` tool_result:
present + `is_error` → `Error`; present → `Completed`; absent → `Running`.

SubagentSummary.description:
Derived aggregate metadata for a spawned subagent, carried on the `Agent`
tool-use content block. Not content — the collapsed `Agent` card renders as
a pure read of this. Shared shape between the read path and the live
`subagentProgress` event (absolute values).

messageCount.description:
`COUNT(*)` of the subagent's rows (rows whose `parent_uuid` equals the
`Agent` tool-use id).

tokens.description: `SUM(input_tokens + output_tokens)` across the subagent's assistant rows.

SubagentTranscriptResponse.description:
Response for GET /tasks/{task_id}/tool-calls/{tool_use_id}/messages — the
on-demand subagent transcript. The assembled, fold-resolved Messages of the
subagent spawned by the given `Agent` tool call.

SyncConfigResponse.description:
Response for `POST /api/v1/repositories/{id}/sync-config`.

Wraps the updated repository plus the loop and workspace reconciliation
summaries. This endpoint is the explicit, user-initiated sync, so it also
reclaims workspaces that were manually overridden — see
[`WorkspaceSyncSummary::reclaimed`].

TagResponse.description: Tag as embedded in a task response (minimal: id + name only).

TaskBindingResponse.description: External adapter binding connected to a task.

TaskBindingSummary.description: External adapter binding summary attached to a task response.

externalThreadId.description: Adapter thread identifier such as GitHub PR number or Slack thread ts.

lastEventAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last event seen on the binding.

subjectKey.description: Adapter-specific subject key such as `owner/repo#123` for GitHub PR bindings.

threadId.description:
Deprecated legacy thread identifier. Canonical callers should use
`binding_id`, which carries the task binding id.

TaskConnectionRow.description: One task and the external connections wired to it.

owner.description: Display name of the task's creator (`None` when unresolved).

TaskConnectionsResponse.description: Paginated list of tasks with their external connections.

TaskEventPayload.description: Task event payload — typed shape for `EventType::Task` events.

TaskEventResponse.description: A single task event in the response.

TaskMessageTokenUsage.description: Token usage attached to a single assistant message.

TaskRelationDto.description: A typed link from one task to another, with optional JSON context.

context.description: Free-form metadata describing why/how the relation was created.

TaskRelationType.description:
Type of a directional link between two tasks. The `from` task points at the
`to` task via this relation (e.g. a child `created_by` its parent).

inactiveTtlDays.description:
Inactive TTL in days. The reaper auto-closes the task when no activity
has occurred for this many days. `0` means "never auto-close".

isFollowing.description:
Whether the requesting user follows this task. Followed tasks appear in
the user's personal task list. `None` when the response was built
without a requesting-user context.

lastReadAt.description:
RFC3339 timestamp of when the requesting user last read this task's
conversation. `None` if they have never opened it. Compare against
`last_message_at` to derive unread state.

parentTaskId.description:
Derived from the `created_by` relation in `relations`. Kept for
backward compatibility with clients that pre-date the relations field.

relations.description: Typed relations this task has to other tasks (currently `created_by`).

sandboxDesiredState.description:
Persisted target state for the task's sandbox. This is application
intent, not live infrastructure status.

sandboxDesiredStateUpdatedAt.description: RFC3339 timestamp for the last desired-state transition.

sandboxStartedAt.description:
RFC3339 timestamp of when the sandbox was last started. `None` if the
task has never had a sandbox running.

oneOf.description: Reason the sandbox was intentionally moved away from `running`, if any.

ttlMinutes.description:
Idle TTL in minutes. The reaper stops the sandbox when no activity has
occurred for this many minutes. `0` means "never reap".

workspaceId.description:
Workspace the task runs in. Every task has one — the insert resolves the
repository's shadow workspace when the creating request named none, and
pre-workspace tasks were backfilled the same way — so this is only
`None` for a response built without reading the persisted row.

workspaceName.description:
Display name for `workspace_id`, resolved alongside `repository_name`.
`None` when the workspace row is deleted or its lookup failed; clients
showing this as a label fall back to the repository.

TaskSkillUsage.description: Skill usage aggregate for a task conversation.

TaskStatisticsResponse.description: Conversation statistics derived from persisted task messages.

toolCallsAvailable.description:
Whether this Task has a tool-call record at all.

A Task that ran before tool calls were stored as their own rows has none,
and an empty `tool_calls` from that Task means "not recorded", not "made
no calls". The client has to be able to tell those apart — reporting zero
is a wrong answer, not a missing one.

Defaults to `true` so a client reading an older response, or a response
from a deployment that predates the field, is not told every Task is
unrecorded.

TaskTokenTotals.description: Aggregate token counts for a task conversation.

TaskToolCallStats.description: Tool-call aggregate for a task conversation.

TaskTurnEventPayload.description: TaskTurn event payload — typed shape for `EventType::TaskTurn` events.

ToolCallDetailResponse.description: Full tool-call detail returned on demand (when a tool call is expanded).

contexts.description:
Contexts attached to this user message (file uploads, preview URLs,
selected elements).

oneOf.description: External source metadata for messages originating from adapters.

hasPendingUserInput.description: Whether this assistant message has pending user input.

messageId.description: Provider message id for assistant rows (e.g. `msg_abc...`).

parentUuid.description: Parent tool use ID (links subagent messages to parent Agent tool call).

sentBy.description:
Moatless user id that authored this message. Absent for system- or
adapter-originated rows (schedulers, bindings, external webhooks,
assistant turns, error results).

sourceTaskId.description: Task ID that sent this message (present for inter-task messages only).

stopReason.description: Provider stop reason for assistant rows (e.g. `end_turn`, `tool_use`).

stopSequence.description: Provider stop sequence for assistant rows, when one was hit.

oneOf.description: Token usage stats for assistant rows.

UiMessageExternalSource.description: External source metadata for messages originating from adapters.

externalId.description:
Stable, type-namespaced external id (e.g. "github:ic:12345",
"slack:ts:1700000.000123"). Present when the row was tagged by an
inbound webhook or by the outbound dedup fix; absent for legacy
rows written before the prefix scheme.

externalLabel.description:
Human-readable rendering of `external_id` (e.g. "Comment #12345",
"PR #42 opened", "ts 1700000.000123"). Falls back to the raw
`external_id` for legacy or unknown prefix shapes.

UiToolResult.description: Tool result inlined into an assistant message.

typedResult.description: Typed tool result from SDK (e.g., BashToolUseResult, ReadToolUseResult).

name.description: Rename the Loop. Omit to keep the current name; a name cannot be cleared.

oneOf.description:
Change the repository's access scope (`global` or `user`).
Re-submitting `user` preserves the repository's existing immutable owner.
An ownerless repository cannot move to `user`.
Requesting `global` requires admin.

UpdateServerConfigRequest.description:
Update one preview server's live config.

Only fields that a sidecar can pick up on an in-place restart are accepted.
`port` and `dockerImage` are declared so a caller that sends them gets an
explicit "redeploy required" instead of a silent no-op.

dockerImage.description: Not applicable live — the image is the container's identity.

env.description: Env entries to set, merged into any existing override.

port.description:
Not applicable live — the port is wired into the Service and
IngressRoute at provision time.

restart.description: Restart the server so the change takes effect (default `true`).

startCommands.description:
Replaces the workspace's start command. Joined with `&&`, as at
provision time.

unsetEnv.description:
Keys to remove from the server's environment. Also drops them from the
override's `env`, so setting and unsetting the same key is coherent.

inactiveTtlDays.description:
New inactivity TTL in days. Must be `>= 0`. `0` disables auto-close for
this task (it stays Open until closed explicitly). Omit to leave the
current inactivity TTL unchanged.

ttlMinutes.description:
New idle TTL in minutes. Must be `>= 0`. `0` disables the idle reaper
for this task (sandbox stays alive until explicitly stopped). Omit to
leave the current idle TTL unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Change the workspace's access scope (`global` or `user`). When set,
`owner_user_id` is re-resolved from the new scope. Requesting `global`
requires admin.

WebhookAccepted.description:
The answer to an accepted delivery.

It names the delivery, not a Task: routing has not run when this is written,
so no Task exists to name yet.

deliveryId.description:
The identity the delivery was admitted under — the caller's own

WebhookAdmission.description: What admission did with a delivery.

deliveryId.description:
Caller-assigned identity for this delivery. Optional, and what it buys
differs sharply by whether it is supplied:

- **Supplied.** Two requests carrying the same `deliveryId` are one
  delivery. The second is recognised as a duplicate and does no further
  work — on any replica, and after any restart.
- **Absent.** A fresh identity is minted per request, so sending the same
  body twice is two deliveries and the work is done twice.

Either way the response means the backend owns the delivery. Only the
deduplication is at the caller's discretion.

It is read from the request body rather than a header because the
signature covers the body only: an identifier carried outside the signed
content could be altered in transit without invalidating the signature,
which would either replay work as new or collapse two distinct
deliveries into one.

WorkspaceRepoInput.description: A repository placement inside a workspace (create/add payload).

branch.description: Override the repository's default branch for this placement.

isPrimary.description:
Mark this placement as the primary (diff/PR/AGENTS.md) repo. At most one
primary is kept per workspace; when several are flagged the first wins.

mountName.description: Subdir under the workspace dir (defaults to the repo name at runtime).

deleted.description:
Soft-deleted workspaces are normally hidden. Git-origin tombstones remain
visible in admin so users can restore them from git without automatic
sync recreating them behind their back.

source.description:
`manual` or `git`. Git-synced workspaces are read-only in the UI and
write API — only a re-sync from git changes them.

sourceConfigPath.description:
Path to the config file within the source repository that declared this
workspace (e.g. `.moatless/workspaces.json` or `.moatless/config.json`).
Retained even after a manual override so the origin remains visible.

sourceKey.description:
The entry's stable key within the declaring file (its `key`, else the
slugified name). Retained after an override, like the other provenance.

sourceRepositoryId.description: The repository whose git tree declared this workspace (`source == "git"`).

WorkspaceSyncSkip.description: One git-declared workspace that was present but not synced, with a reason.

WorkspaceSyncSummary.description: Summary of reconciling a repo's git-declared workspaces into `workspaces`.

reclaimed.description:
Manually overridden workspaces taken back under git control by an
explicit sync, discarding the local edits.

removed.description: Workspaces soft-deleted because git no longer declares them.

skipped.description: Workspaces that were declared but not synced, with reasons.

updated.description: Existing git-synced workspaces updated in place.
